prior_summary: Role-conditioned noninterference in a learned action diffusion model: a TCP/red/blue interaction graph estimates passive versus active roles, and an action-conditioned ensemble provides masked preservation and conservative point-to-cube clearance training losses. The fixed sampler has no candidate-ranking hook; ranking is not implemented and preservation is amortized into the epsilon predictor during training.
applicable_conditions: Two observed 0.04 m cubes on the known world table, original Panda joint/gripper dynamics and fixed world goals. The complete expanded transfer_blue slice includes closed-grip red descent into the buffer, release and retreat, blue acquisition/transport/placement, and retreat followed by red retrieval/lift. Requires two causal 47-dimensional states including joint positions/velocities, aperture, TCP and both object poses. Active roles depend on observed association and motion, not color alone. Spatial support is limited to demonstrated sites and routes.
termination_guidance: Use observation-based continuation, not elapsed steps. During incoming overlap continue red descent/release before treating red as passive. After blue is supported near its goal, this policy can continue opening, retreating and retrieving red. A useful exit has blue at its goal and red rising with close TCP association and total finger width near 0.0365 m; hand off the measured state to finish_red without reopening or returning toward blue. Blue reaching a geometric goal alone is not the same as a completed manipulation transition. These are handoff cues, not extra task-success predicates.
limitations: Successful demonstrations do not calibrate collisions or recovery. Weak role labels infer association/support without contact sensing. Forward models may ignore unsafe actions or predict passive stationarity regardless of action; ensemble agreement is not evidence of safety. The clearance term models a TCP point against an oriented cube, not fingers, links or held-object geometry. There is no inference candidate generation/ranking, likelihood estimator, online guidance, IK, FK, hard constraint, symmetry guarantee, or image encoder. Two observations cannot resolve all dwell/contact ambiguities. Roles and auxiliary losses require ablation and performance is unmeasured.

architecture.edge_features: directed shared-scale relative displacement and norm, both role probabilities, both node embeddings
architecture.dynamics_outputs: 16 future red/blue poses and TCP positions, residual to current observed state
architecture.deployment: single fixed DDPM sample, learned causal role-conditioned epsilon network

normalization.relational_position_scale: shared normalizer std[18:21], the complete-demo TCP half ranges
normalization.quaternions: wxyz unit components; sign-invariant auxiliary orientation error
normalization.action_representation: shared affinely normalized seven absolute joint targets and gripper command
normalization.time_features: backward displacement per observation; no unprovided sample period or elapsed phase

auxiliary_gradient_control.guidance_world_model_weights: detached; expert fit trains them separately
auxiliary_gradient_control.guidance_world_condition: detached; gradients to denoised actions remain
auxiliary_gradient_control.trust: detached exp(-expert ensemble position variance / 0.02^2 - expert mean position error / 0.02^2)
auxiliary_gradient_control.padding: action and future masks; no future outside assigned slice

config.coverage_semantics: start inclusive, stop exclusive for actions; terminal observation at stop; metadata is evidence of coverage, never an inference schedule
